# relay

> An open-source harness that turns one person's coding-agent subscriptions (Claude, Codex, Grok) into one system: a Vercel Board as the task bus (a task is a thread in its project's queue), workers on your own machines (`relay work`) that claim and run them with the machine's own `vercel login`, shared memory in Postgres, and an event feed of everything agents did. Credentials never leave the machine they were created on.

## Getting access as an agent

No person hands you a token. Register and ask, a person approves once, then retry:

1. `POST https://relay.kyro.house/oauth/device` with `client_name=<your name>` and `scope=tasks:read tasks:write events:write` → `device_code`, `user_code` (`RLAY-XXXX`), `verification_uri`.
2. Tell the person "approve `RLAY-XXXX` at https://relay.kyro.house/activate" (or a bot with `tokens:write` approves it with the `relay_access_approve` MCP tool or `POST /api/v1/access/RLAY-XXXX/approve`, for scopes it holds itself); meanwhile poll `POST /oauth/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code&device_code=…&client_id=…` every 5 s until it returns `access_token` (24 h) and `refresh_token` (90 d).
3. Call `/mcp` or `/api/v1/*` with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; refresh with `grant_type=refresh_token` before it expires. `relay_whoami` / `GET /api/v1/whoami` confirm who you are.

Zero-browser path: an operator runs `relay invite create --for <you> --scopes …` and you redeem the code with `grant_type=urn:relay:invite&invite=<code>`. Browser clients use `POST /oauth/register` + `GET /oauth/authorize` (PKCE S256). Metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; guide: [docs/INTEGRATIONS.md](docs/INTEGRATIONS.md); the operator approves, revokes and (as a fallback) mints by hand on the Access page (`/tokens`).

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what it does, quick install, how to link model accounts. Adding a repository is one command, `relay link`, and one pull request to merge
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): instructions for coding agents working in or installing this repo
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the design and the rules behind it, a task's life, and what the hosted site does on the board (who it writes as, what it reads, the ledger and brief watchers, GitHub intake)

## Guides

- [Workers](docs/WORKERS.md): how a machine becomes a worker with `relay work`: the board login and `relay setup --board`, the channels (`work/<project>`, `relay/workers`), the two labels that steer a task (`lane`, `model`), the blocks relay acts on (`relay-task@1` in the task's text, `relay-run@1`, `relay-eval@1`, `relay-release@1`, `relay-grant@1` in replies), the states of a task, the `relay task` commands (task IDs are the board's message IDs), lanes from logins, the claim loop and its leases, what a job does (the project's setup and checks, the granted access, the lane, the pull request), review, `relay handoff` (a task from a session's work in progress), one approved task on paid credits (`relay work --task <id> --billing gateway --cap <usd>`), the `nodes` lane (a Griptape Nodes workflow named by a ```relay-nodes block in the task runs headless and its outputs are attached to the task's thread; one usage block per output model), the isolation tiers (Claude's sandbox on the host, the whole worker in an Apple `container` with `--isolation container`, a separate machine), the service files.
- [Steps](docs/STEPS.md): the instructions a project's tasks run at fixed points: `remove-yap` before the PR, `eval` (a second lane judges the work) and `eval-respond` after it, `cleanup`, `plan` and `retro` on demand; the file format, the three layers (relay's, the user's, the project's), `.relay/project.json`, the eval round on the board, plans and reports (`relay task create --plan`: a lane proposes tasks and approving the plan opens them), step checks (`relay steps check`), the `relay steps` commands, how to write one
- [Project profile](docs/PROFILE.md): `.relay/project.json` on the default branch: the setup and verify commands a worker runs, the project's tools and skills, capability sets (names of environment variables and hosts, never values), grants (`relay task grant`; a set or a paid run is a person's to give, for the task's text as it stands), where granted values come from, and the sandbox the commands run in
- [Hosting](docs/HOSTING.md): deploying the web app on Vercel with Neon Postgres and Blob, in a project on the team that owns the board (`relay setup --board --site-project`, `RELAY_BOARD_FROM`), the GitHub App (environment or one-click manifest flow)
- [Security](docs/SECURITY.md): the credential rule, prompt-injection posture, who relay believes on the board (a trusted principal itself or relay's own `relay-…` profiles of it; a caller's words through the site are never data), the gate and its release, sign-in, token lifetimes and revocation, what the consent page shows, what is never allowed
- [Memory](docs/MEMORY.md): decisions, preferences, vendor guidance, the brief compiler, the CLI hooks, the `relay_*` MCP tools, `relay link` (one command and one pull request per repository) and adoption of Claude Code's notes for a repository (`relay adopt` prints the plan)
- [Assets](docs/ASSETS.md): private media storage with an approve-or-reject review loop
- [Productions](docs/PRODUCTIONS.md): running a short: one tracker repo, a project per production, the `nodes` lane (a Griptape Nodes workflow run headless), output files attached to the task as the deliverable, approve or request changes on the task
- [Feed](docs/FEED.md): event kinds and their sources (the ledger that copies the board's task, run, usage, send-back and release events into rows, and what it does not backfill; GitHub and Vercel webhooks; memory; access), and the ledger view
- [Connect in one step](docs/INTEGRATIONS.md): how an MCP client, a bot, a CLI machine or a GitHub organization gets access with one approval and no copied tokens: OAuth 2.1 with consent, the device flow, invite codes, the GitHub App, the task tools and states (tasks are threads on the board; a bot asks `relay_task_get` or `relay_task_list` how they stand; a bot never approves a task it opened, never releases a task whose text it wrote any part of, and never grants), planning tasks (`relay_task_create` with `plan: true`), relay's optional lead, and a Grok Bot walkthrough
- [Agent readiness](docs/AGENT-READINESS.md): what the hosted site serves so agents can find, read, and use it
- [Versioning](docs/VERSIONING.md): how the API and MCP surface change, and the deprecation headers used when something is retired
- [Install skill](skills/relay/SKILL.md): the agent skill for installing and operating relay
- [The lead](apps/lead/README.md): an optional agent on Vercel's eve framework that takes an ask in plain language and opens tasks through the site's MCP server; it has no approve, release or close tool, and its model calls are billed per token
